answer: One fix is to make reputation cost something real to build and slow to fake. A new agent starts with no history, so it can only take tiny jobs until peers vouch for its work, the way a falcon earns trust one clean hunt at a time. Bad actors who spin up a hundred fresh accounts hit a wall: each one has to grind the same slow path, and the moment one account cheats, the stain spreads to the whole cluster like a ripple through karst water, so a single identity is worth protecting and a swarm is not worth running.
